narrative:
The model estimates a 76% chance that you will leave your current role, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system has learned from many similar employee profiles.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current organization, and the other job offers you have received. 

Your 11 or more years of total professional experience is relatively uncommon among people the model expects to stay; most who remain have between one and ten years. This longer career history pushed the prediction toward leaving. Similarly, having spent only one to five years in your present role—while typical for those predicted to stay—still added to the likelihood of departure in your specific combination of circumstances. Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities worked in the same direction, as external offers often signal that someone is actively considering or being pulled toward new options.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model associates with higher turnover risk. 

Your organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as clearer promotion paths, better recognition of your long experience, or addressing the external opportunities that attracted you. You may also want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your career goals.
